summary: Dynamic resonance suppressor working on a short-time spectrum (2048-point frames, hop a quarter of that): each frequency is compared with a reference, and where it stands out the machine turns that narrow region down for as long as it does, so harsh ringing, boxiness and sibilant peaks are smoothed without a fixed EQ. Suppress compares each bin with the spectrum around it, Balance moves the whole spectrum toward a pink slope (with a tilt), Stabilize pulls the short-term spectrum toward its own long-term average. Depth, Knee, Selectivity and Smoothing shape what counts as a resonance; Lift lets it also fill dips. Region keeps it to a frequency range, Mix and Delta (hear only what it takes out) check it. The latency is the frame (43 ms at 44.1 and 48 kHz, reported). Use it on a vocal, a guitar, a mix bus or a master for harshness and resonances that move.
use_for: Smooth harsh resonances that move: a dynamic, spectrum-wide suppressor for vocals, guitars, buses and masters.

parameters.name: Mode
parameters.description: Suppress: each bin against the spectrum around it. Balance: the whole spectrum against a pink slope plus Tilt. Stabilize: the short-term spectrum against its own long-term average (4 s)
parameters.how: Chooses what the spectrum is compared with: its neighbourhood (Suppress), a pink slope (Balance) or its own long-term average (Stabilize).
parameters.sound: Suppress calms narrow, ringing peaks; Balance evens out an overall tonal tilt; Stabilize keeps a part of the spectrum from jumping out from moment to moment.

parameters.name: Depth
parameters.description: How much of what stands out is taken out: 100 % brings it to the reference
parameters.how: Sets how much of the excess over the reference is removed, from 0 to 100 %.
parameters.sound: Low values tame resonances gently; 100 % removes them completely and can sound hollow.

parameters.name: Knee
parameters.description: How far over the reference a bin must stand before it is acted on (softly: little below, nearly full above)
parameters.how: Sets how far a frequency must stand out before the machine reacts, from 1 to 10 dB.
parameters.sound: A low knee also touches ordinary variation and can dull the sound; a high one only catches clear resonances.

parameters.name: Selectivity
parameters.description: Half-width of the neighbourhood a bin is compared with, in octaves (Suppress, and the smoothing of Balance)
parameters.how: Sets how wide the reference neighbourhood is, from 0.1 to 1 octave.
parameters.sound: Narrow values catch only needle-thin peaks; wide ones also catch broad bumps in the tone.

parameters.name: Smoothing
parameters.description: Widens the cut across neighbouring frequencies (each bin is 23 Hz at 48 kHz)
parameters.how: Spreads each cut over neighbouring frequency bins, from 0 to 6.
parameters.sound: Larger values make the cuts broader and softer; 0 gives the narrowest, most surgical notches.

parameters.name: Tilt
parameters.description: Balance only: slope added to the pink target above 300 Hz
parameters.how: Tilts the Balance target above 300 Hz, from -6 to +6 dB per octave.
parameters.sound: Positive values aim for a brighter balance, negative for a darker one.

parameters.name: Lift
parameters.description: How much a dip below the reference may be filled in (0: cut only)
parameters.how: Sets how far the machine may raise frequencies that sit below the reference, from 0 to 12 dB.
parameters.sound: At 0 it only cuts; a few dB fill holes and even out the tone but can also lift noise.

parameters.name: Attack
parameters.description: How fast a cut comes in (faster at high frequencies)
parameters.how: Sets how fast a cut comes in, from 2 ms to 200 ms (faster in the highs).
parameters.sound: Short attacks catch a resonance as it starts; long ones leave the start of each note untouched.

parameters.name: Release
parameters.description: How fast a cut lets go (faster at high frequencies)
parameters.how: Sets how fast a cut lets go, from 20 ms to 2 s (faster in the highs).
parameters.sound: Short releases follow the signal closely; long ones are smoother and more stable.

parameters.name: Low limit
parameters.description: Below this frequency nothing is changed
parameters.how: Sets the lowest frequency the machine works on, from 40 Hz to 4 kHz.
parameters.sound: Raise it to keep the bass and the body of the sound untouched.

parameters.name: High limit
parameters.description: Above this frequency nothing is changed
parameters.how: Sets the highest frequency the machine works on, from 2 kHz to 20 kHz.
parameters.sound: Lower it to keep the air and the top end untouched.

parameters.name: Mix
parameters.description: Wet against dry; at 0 % the output is the delayed input, bit for bit
parameters.how: Blends the processed signal with the dry one (delayed to match).
parameters.sound: Parallel use keeps the character of the source while the suppression still smooths it.

parameters.name: Output
parameters.description: Gain after the suppressor, 0.1 dB steps (the editor's Match sets it from the gain-match reading)
parameters.how: Adds -24 to +24 dB of gain after the suppressor.
parameters.sound: It matches the loudness to the untreated signal so you can judge the tone fairly.

parameters.name: Delta
parameters.description: Hear only what the suppressor takes out: the output minus the input, delayed to match (glides over 10 ms)
parameters.how: Plays only the difference between the output and the input.
parameters.sound: You hear exactly what is being removed, so you can check it is resonance and not the body of the sound.

readings.description: The deepest cut now, dB (0 or more)
The mean cut over the working region now, dB (0 or more)
The frame, N − 1 (2047 at 44.1 and 48 kHz), reported to NeoBuzz Live
